cards.front: According to the DSM-5-TR, which diagnostic code should be used to document a patient's non-adherence to medical treatment?
What is the primary clinical rationale for using Long-Acting Injectable (LAI) antipsychotics in patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders?
cards.back: To ensure treatment adherence and prevent early psychotic relapse (StahlNeuro p. 233, Dulcan p. 402).

cards.front: What neurobiological consequence is associated with each successive episode of psychotic relapse?
cards.back: Relapses are associated with a cumulative loss of brain tissue volume and increased resistance to future treatment (StahlNeuro p. 162, Dulcan p. 402).

cards.front: Why is a $21$-day (3-week) oral antipsychotic overlap mandatory when initiating Risperidone Consta?
cards.back: There is a significant lag time before the polymer microspheres release therapeutic levels of the medication into the bloodstream (StahlKids p. 42, StahlNeuro p. 234).

cards.front: Which LAI antipsychotic requires a $14$-day oral overlap period following the first injection?
How does the initiation protocol for Invega Sustenna (Paliperidone Palmitate) eliminate the need for oral overlap?
cards.back: It utilizes a rapid-loading dose in the deltoid muscle followed by a second dose one week later (StahlNeuro p. 234, Source 5).

cards.front: What is the required duration of clinical stability on Invega Sustenna before a patient can transition to the 3-month Invega Trinza formulation?
cards.back: A minimum of $4$ consecutive months of proven stability and tolerability (StahlKids p. 370, StahlNeuro p. 234).

cards.front: When converting from Invega Sustenna to Invega Trinza, the 3-month dose is calculated by multiplying the last monthly dose by _____.
Which first-generation antipsychotic is FDA-approved for the treatment of schizophrenia in pediatric patients as young as $3$ years old?
Patients receiving Olanzapine Relprevv must be monitored for $3$ hours post-injection to detect which potentially severe complication?
Which three Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes are most critical for the clearance of the majority of antipsychotic medications?
Paliperidone carries a lower risk of drug-drug interactions because less than _____ percent of the drug undergoes first-pass hepatic metabolism.
Initiation of Clozapine requires a baseline Absolute Neutrophil Count (ANC) of at least _____ in the general population.
Which side effect, characterized by inner restlessness and an inability to remain still, is a common $D_{2}$ blockade-related risk in pediatric patients?
The mechanism of Aripiprazole involves partial agonism at $D_{2}$ and $5-HT_{1A}$ receptors, combined with antagonism at the _____ receptor.
What is the recommended injection interval for Haloperidol Decanoate?
Which enzyme is responsible for storing monoamines and histamine in synaptic vesicles and is the target of treatments for tardive dyskinesia?
How do LAI antipsychotics reduce the side-effect profile compared to irregular oral dosing?
cards.back: They eliminate the sharp "peak-to-trough" fluctuations in plasma drug levels associated with inconsistent pill-taking (StahlNeuro p. 233).

cards.front: In pediatric patients, why are more frequent dosing or higher weight-based doses often required compared to adults?
cards.back: Physiological developmental differences result in faster drug clearance and metabolism in children and adolescents (Dulcan p. 785).

cards.front: According to Dulcan's textbook, what is the status of systematic research on LAI antipsychotics in youth?
cards.back: LAI forms of antipsychotics have not been systematically studied in children and adolescents (Dulcan p. 402).
